kicker: Small and mid-size manufacturers and distributors
lede: Thirty small agents that check a manufacturer's or distributor's back office from the files it already exports, work order costs, purchasing, inventory, production, retail and EDI compliance, quality and safety, and wait for a named person before anything is posted, paid, shipped or sent.
packages: Standard against actual by work order, purchase price variance, BOM roll-up, overhead absorption, WIP aging, job margins, landed cost (7 agents)
BOM and routing gaps, scrap and yield, labor efficiency, machine downtime, capacity load, preventive maintenance (6 agents)
Cycle counts, slow-moving and obsolete stock, shelf life, reorder points, lot traceability (5 agents)
Late purchase orders, supplier scorecards, rebates and price agreements, material certificates (4 agents)
Order backlog, retailer deductions, ASN errors, invoices against customer orders, set to one trading partner's guide (4 agents)
Calibration due dates, NCR and CAPA aging, injury log completeness, tariff code consistency (4 agents)
All 30 agents mapped to your exports and set to your rules, one training session
Whole plant for each plant on one ERP, mapped once, each plant with its own settings
For accounting firms, fractional controllers, ERP consultants and 3PLs serving many manufacturers: all 30 agents, one shared setup, every client mapped
support: Support after setup: $200 a month for one pack, $450 a month for the whole plant, $300 a month per plant for multi-plant, $1,200 a month for a partner rollout. Includes export changes, setting updates, new versions and a monthly check-in.
notes: Reads the files you export; it does not log in to your ERP, MES, EDI network, bank or customer portals.
Export layouts were written from knowledge of each system and are confirmed on your files during setup; none was tested against a live account.
Tolerances, retailer fines and dispute windows, material specs, tariff code lists and injury-log day caps are your settings; the agents do not know any customer's, agency's or standard's rules.
Not legal, tax, customs, safety or accounting advice: the agents do not classify goods or decide whether an injury is recordable.
Report pages can be in nine languages; the translations are Claude's and have not been reviewed by native speakers.
warn: Your files and reports stay on your computer. The agents never post to the ERP, pay, ship, change a standard or schedule, release a hold, transmit EDI, file with an agency or message anyone: each of those is refused or waits for one named person's click. Employee names are masked in anything sent to an AI model.
groups: Material, labor and overhead variance on every work order, and orders closed with cost and no output
Receipt prices against standard, price jumps from the same supplier, unit-of-measure slips
Every assembly costed from its bill of materials and the latest prices, against its standard
Overhead applied to jobs against overhead spent, by work center, with proposed rates
Work in process by age, stale orders, and closed orders still holding WIP
Quoted against actual cost and invoiced amount for every job
Freight, duty and brokerage bills matched to receipts and to what was put into item cost
Made items with no BOM or routing, inactive components, zero quantities, loops
Scrap against each item's standard, with the cost of the excess, by work center and reason
Standard hours earned against hours clocked, by work center, never by person
Availability, MTTR and MTBF from MES exports, recurring stop reasons
Open operation hours by week against each work center's available hours
PM tasks overdue by date or run hours, with a calendar of due dates
Counts against system quantity with tolerances by ABC class, and repeat variances
Stock by months since it moved and months of supply, with a reserve proposal
Expired stock, short-dated shipments and first-expired-first-out misses
Stockouts, stock under safety stock and reorder points that no longer fit usage
Breaks in the lot and serial chain from receipt through production to shipment
Open lines past due, never confirmed, or promised after production needs them
On-time delivery, rejects in ppm and price against PO, weighted and ranked
Rebate tiers reached and not claimed, and purchases above the agreed price
Certificates missing, for another heat, or outside your purchase specs
Open order lines past their promise date, never promised, or promised later than asked
Deductions and chargebacks checked against your ASN and delivery records, with dispute dates
Ship notices (856) against customer orders (850) and shipments: missing, late, wrong quantities
Invoices (810) priced or counted differently from the customer's PO
Gauges overdue or due soon, and work orders measured with a suspect gauge
Open nonconformances, overdue or unverified corrective actions, repeat defects
Missing fields, day counts that contradict the outcome, privacy cases with names
Missing or conflicting tariff codes, origins and duty rates across your own records
closing: Each one does one job, on your computer, from a file you export. Nothing is posted, paid, shipped or sent until a named person on your team says so.
